title: She Makes $40K/Month with This Weird Hawaiian Dessert
promo_conflict: Promotional business-profile framing; no paid placement or other commercial relationship is disclosed.

stated_problem.quote: So I think in today's day and age, people are looking for die-free, preservative-free, quality ingredients, and it can be hard to find that.
stated_problem.speaker: Stephanie

idea.name: Hawaiian shave-ice shop
idea.one_liner: A local dessert shop sells made-to-order Hawaiian shave ice with fresh syrups and toppings at per-serving prices.
idea.customer: Local residents and visitors looking for a fresh, higher-quality frozen dessert.
idea.offer: Shaved ice with ice cream, house-made syrups and toppings, served at a fixed location with outdoor seating.
idea.revenue_model: Retail sales per serving; seasonal specials and higher-priced larger servings.

key_quotes.quote: So we're open Friday, Saturday and Sunday in the winter time.
We have about 10 different syrups that we make.
For us, we have utilized our local content creators. They are amazing.
I just invite them for free product.

claims.claim: The host says the shop brings in $40,000 a month and is less than three years old.
claims.quote: Her tiny shave eye shot brings in $40,000 a month, and it's less than three years old.

claims.claim: The host says busy months can bring in up to $95,000.
claims.quote: Busy months can bring in up to $95,000.

claims.claim: The shop opened in October 2023.
claims.quote: So we opened October of 2023.

claims.claim: They spent eight to nine months testing and perfecting the menu before opening.
claims.quote: I mean, there is a good eight to nine month period of us testing and perfecting our menu.

claims.claim: The shop opens Friday, Saturday and Sunday during winter.
claims.quote: So we're open Friday, Saturday and Sunday in the winter time.

claims.claim: They make about 10 different syrups.
claims.quote: We have about 10 different syrups that we make.

claims.claim: The host describes nine months of R&D before any sales.
claims.quote: Nine months, R&Ding, every flavor, shaving ice, without selling a single ice cream or shaved ice.

claims.claim: Stephanie advises adding 10 to 15% to a build-out estimate.
claims.quote: You have to like add 10 to 15% on a build-out.

claims.claim: One serving can include three syrups.
claims.quote: Well, it depends. So this one has three cereps in it.

claims.claim: Stephanie says her fastest serving time was under one minute.
claims.quote: The fastest I've done would be, it was definitely under a minute, right?

claims.claim: Syrup cost for the example serving was estimated at about five cents.
claims.quote: What are the cost of this one right here? The cost of goods is roughly. These cereps are going to be maybe five cents or something like that.

claims.claim: The host states a selling price of about $12 to $13.
claims.quote: Selling this for about 12 to $13.

claims.claim: A small serving is $9.50 and a large is $11.50.
claims.quote: So a small one's going to be nine dollars and 50 cents. And then a large one is going to be 11.50.

claims.claim: Monthly special servings are $11.50 small and $13.50 large.
claims.quote: And then if it's one of our special products that we always do specials every month, that's going to be 11.50 for a small one and 13.50 for a larger one.

claims.claim: Stephanie says the best month was either July or August, at around $95,000.
claims.quote: I believe it was either July or August and we hit right around 95K.

claims.claim: The $95,000 month occurred in the second summer, about a year and a half after opening.
claims.quote: So that was in our second summer. It was really about a year and a half because we opened in October the previous year.

claims.claim: The host and owners state the shop accounts for 85% and the truck 15% of revenue.
claims.quote: I'd say 85% the store, 15% the truck.

claims.quote: What do we have for total? So we're at 408.5?

claims.quote: For a call? P&L is at 79.5?

claims.quote: I mean, I would want to be in the, you know, grow by 20% so the 500 rate 500 plus.

claims.quote: Very seasonal. You go from almost one to like what? Mid-20s at some point, just to handle the business?

claims.quote: I think last year is 25.

claims.quote: Seven days a week. Also if we're running the food truck, then that's a whole nother team that has to be involved.

claims.claim: The host refers to a $60,000 startup estimate; Stephanie says the build-out cost about double their estimate.
claims.quote: 60K, you spent double that to audience, what happened?

claims.claim: Stephanie says the build-out doubled from the expected starting cost as they discovered more work.
claims.quote: So that kind of doubled in price from where we thought it was the starting point was, and then once we really dug into what we needed to do, it just started going up and up and up.

acquisition_channels.details: They invite local content creators to try the product for free; the creators have concentrated local audiences.
They collaborate with local people, including a photographer, on special flavors.
Customers visit the fixed shop and eat at its outdoor seating.

ideas.delivery: Stephanie and staff prepare each serving in the shop using shaved ice, ice cream, house-made syrups and toppings. Customers are served at the counter and use outdoor seating.

prices: about $0.05 syrup cost for the example serving
platforms: Google (mentioned as a source for syrup-making information)

ideas.other_uk_rules: A UK shop would need food-business registration, food hygiene controls and allergen information. UK GDPR applies if customer details are used for marketing; gifted creator content may need clear advertising disclosure. Seasonal hiring brings UK right-to-work, minimum-wage and working-time requirements; Employment Agencies Regulations 2003 matter if agency staff are used.

idea.name: Seasonal shave-ice food truck
idea.one_liner: A mobile truck sells shave ice at events and seasonal locations, earning per-serving revenue with a staffed crew.
idea.customer: Event visitors, beachgoers and local consumers.
idea.offer: Made-to-order Hawaiian shave ice from a wrapped food truck during the summer season.
idea.revenue_model: Retail sales per serving at events and mobile locations.

key_quotes.quote: Right now, it's just a location for a brick and mortar, and then we also have a food truck that we run during the summertime.
So you can only be in one spot for a certain amount of time. You cannot stay there.
So a food truck is definitely a lower cost of entry than a brick and mortar and a full build out.
The truck came set up for a Boba shop.

claims.claim: The owners initially thought they would start with a food truck.
claims.quote: So we 100% thought we were going to be a food truck to start.

claims.claim: They report average event staffing of three people and a busy crew of four.
claims.quote: On any given event, I would say like average is three. Our busy busy is four.

claims.claim: The truck cost about $21,000 and its wrap about $8,000.
claims.quote: The truck cost was probably like 21. And then the wrap was probably eight. I want to say grand, okay.

acquisition_channels.details: They sell directly to walk-up customers at events and permitted locations.
The owner says truck locations and permitted time at each spot are restricted in Virginia Beach.

ideas.delivery: The owners and a seasonal crew prepare and sell shave ice from a wrapped, already-fitted truck. The truck runs in summer; staffing it requires a separate team.

platforms: Virginia Beach Oceanfront boardwalk (mentioned as a potential cart location)

ideas.other_uk_rules: A UK mobile food business would need food-business registration, food hygiene and allergen controls, plus any local street-trading consent, event permission and vehicle requirements. Seasonal employment rules apply; Employment Agencies Regulations 2003 are relevant if agency staff are supplied.

idea.name: Shave-ice cart
idea.one_liner: A lower-cost cart sells a small menu of shave-ice flavors to walk-up customers and lets an operator test local demand.
idea.customer: Beachgoers, tourists and other local consumers.
idea.offer: A cart with shaved ice, syrups and a limited flavor selection.

key_quotes.quote: Even cheaper way that I would say to start this type of business would be a food cart.
A really good way to start would be having a cart.
So you would have your eyes, you would have some syrups, you don't have to go crazy with the flavor, but you can get some full, maybe five different flavors.

claims.claim: Stephanie suggests starting with about five flavors.
claims.quote: So you would have your eyes, you would have some syrups, you don't have to go crazy with the flavor, but you can get some full, maybe five different flavors.

acquisition_channels.details: Sell to walk-up customers at a boardwalk or another suitable local location.

ideas.delivery: The operator prepares and sells shave ice directly from a cart; a limited menu is suggested as a way to test demand.
ideas.other_uk_rules: UK food-business registration, hygiene and allergen controls apply; a selling location may also require local street-trading consent and landowner permission.

stated_problem.quote: No one wants to wear Virginia Beach Shave Ice or a T-shirt, right?
stated_problem.speaker: Todd

idea.name: Get Lost branded merchandise
idea.one_liner: The shave-ice brand sells branded apparel to customers in-store and through a small number of online orders.
idea.customer: Shop visitors and fans of the Get Lost brand.
idea.offer: Branded shirts, sweatshirts, tank tops and other apparel.
idea.revenue_model: Retail sales of apparel, mostly in person, with occasional online orders.

key_quotes.quote: I didn't want that because we wanted something that we could sell merch.
No one wants to wear Virginia Beach Shave Ice or a T-shirt, right?
You can buy it online when we get very few orders online.

claims.claim: Todd says merchandise contributes about 20% of business revenue.
claims.quote: It's probably close to 20%.

claims.claim: They report merchandise margins of 50% to 60%.
claims.quote: Our margins are 50 to 60%.

claims.claim: A $60 sweatshirt is compared with roughly six shave-ice servings in sales volume.
claims.quote: If you think about it, you sell a $60 sweatshirt. You've got to sell six shavers. Roughly six shavers to do that.

claims.claim: The host speculates that a $23,000 P&L line is merchandise cost of goods; confirmation is unclear in the transcript.
claims.quote: I'm assuming that that's a cost of goods for merch. But 23K?

acquisition_channels.details: Most merchandise is bought by customers who visit for shave ice.
They accept a small number of online orders; the online platform is not named.

ideas.delivery: Apparel is displayed and sold at the shop, including a seasonal merchandise shed, with a few orders sold online. The transcript does not name the manufacturer or online platform.
ideas.other_uk_rules: UK online apparel sales would need to follow consumer distance-selling and returns rules; UK GDPR applies to customer data used for online orders or marketing. Product and textile labeling requirements may apply.
